ordered_tracks: optional federated collection index and exact planner
bounded-memory cohort execution and sparse streaming output

collection.artifact: derived, rebuildable, versioned sidecar; authoritative evidence remains in standalone .aie archives
required: global junction catalogue with sample presence and support upper bounds
strict deterministic construction and malformed-input rejection
exact region, junction, and junction-set answers relative to naive archive federation
forbidden: annotation-, PolyASite-, or cell-group-dependent state in authoritative archives
silently accepting duplicate archives or mixed references
approximating exact molecule or cell counts from support upper bounds

gates.exactness: byte- or value-identical answers for synthetic adversarial cases and frozen real queries
gates.determinism: two builds from the same manifest are byte-identical
gates.metadata_only_build: collection construction does not decode molecule chunks
gates.size: sidecar no larger than 5 percent of aggregate archive bytes
gates.latency: no more than 10 percent regression on the existing six-archive targeted query and measurable pruning on a sparse multi-archive panel
gates.incrementality: adding a segment does not rewrite existing segments and gives the same logical catalogue as a clean rebuild

required: memory bounded by an active chromosome or gene shard rather than total cohort molecules
same cross-fitted kernels, EM arithmetic, recurrence, inference, and row ordering
versioned sparse output with explicit dimensions so omitted rows reconstruct as logical zeros
streaming conversion to interoperable columnar output when the dependency cost is acceptable

gates.identity: sites.tsv, genes.tsv, and fragment-kernel.tsv remain byte-identical
gates.memory: maximum RSS at most 2.25 GiB on the frozen eight-donor workload
gates.runtime: wall time at most 30 seconds on the frozen host
gates.output: large federated event output at least 4-fold smaller than the current pushed-down JSON without losing schema fields or zero semantics

adaptive_frontier.status: optional archive-v2 pilot; default two-representative mode remains unchanged until promotion
adaptive_frontier.definition: retain a deterministic annotation-independent antichain of nondominated read geometries within each molecule junction chain, plus exact chain multiplicity

gates.format_safety: explicit layout/version guard and malformed-frontier rejection
gates.storage: no more than 5 percent archive-size premium for a promoted default
gates.accuracy: at least 20 percent relative improvement in the principal incomplete-chain velocity discrepancy or at least 25 percent relative improvement in Gene replay discrepancy, with no component worsening by more than 0.25 percentage point
gates.theory: state and test the preserved predicate class; publish counterexamples outside it

terminal_tail.status: optional sparse pilot; absence of tail evidence is never interpreted as evidence of absence
terminal_tail.stored_fields: only oriented terminal soft-clip tail evidence and its genomic anchor/confidence; never general sequence or qualities

gates.default_regression: archive bytes and replay are unchanged when disabled
gates.storage: no more than 2 percent archive-size premium and target below 0.5 bit per input read
gates.orientation: synthetic forward/reverse and clipped/unclipped cases are exact
gates.accuracy: tail-positive evidence is enriched at external PolyASite candidates versus matched noncandidate/internal-priming controls in at least three independent 3-prime datasets
gates.utility: held-out candidate discrimination or calibration improves in at least three datasets; otherwise retain only as an audit, not an archive feature

claim_guards: Collection support totals are routing bounds, not cell-group counts.
A fragment endpoint is not a cleavage site.
An adaptive evidence frontier is sufficient only for the explicitly proved predicate class.
Negative or underpowered pilots remain recorded and cannot be rescued by relaxing gates after inspection.
